requirement:
A requirement or example judgment MUST use one of these outcomes, applying
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`:

- `true`: the sources support the subject and its testing obligations.
- `false`: the sources do not support the subject, or information is missing,
  and the gaps are not all explicitly acknowledged in source comments or tests.
- `FIXME`: some aspects remain unmet or untested, and source comments or tests
  explicitly acknowledge those gaps. The reviewer MUST explain the gaps and
  their source locations in the rationale and record their issue references or
  other identifying content from the inputs.

The JSON `determination` MUST be `true`, `false`, or an object containing exactly
`"FIXME"` with a nonempty array of nonempty strings, such as
`{"FIXME": ["#125", "rust-lang/rust#123"]}`. The expected source convention is
`FIXME(issue-number)`, for example `FIXME(#125)` or
`FIXME(rust-lang/rust#123)`. References MAY appear elsewhere in the comment or
test; the reviewer MUST recognize explicit acknowledgments without requiring
that spelling. When no issue reference is present, the strings MUST identify the
documented gap using its source content. A FIXME judgment MUST be grounded in
recorded evidence inputs; a bare issue reference without an acknowledged gap
MUST NOT suffice.
rationale:
**Judgment: `requirements.ci.outcomes` is satisfied.**

The requirement has two parts. One is a data contract: the JSON `determination` is `true`, `false`, or an object with exactly `FIXME` holding a nonempty array of nonempty strings. The other is reviewer guidance: when to choose each outcome, and what a FIXME rationale must contain.

**Implementation**
- `src/judgment.rs`:
  - `enum Judgment` has exactly the three outcomes.
  - `Judgment::from_value` accepts only `true`, `false`, or a single-key `FIXME` object whose value is a nonempty array of non-blank strings. It rejects null, strings, bare arrays, `{}`, extra keys, wrong-case keys, empty or blank entries, and non-string entries.
  - `Judgment::to_value` round-trips the three shapes.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs`:
  - `tool_definitions_with` advertises the `submit_judgment` schema as a `oneOf` of a boolean and a `FIXME` object. The object has `additionalProperties:false`, a required `FIXME` array with `minItems:1`, and items with `minLength:1`.
  - `tool_definitions` is the `#[cfg(test)]` wrapper around it.
  - `initial_prompt` fills the template that carries the guidance on when to choose each outcome. The template is in `md/requirements/authoring.md`, section "Prompt template". It says to choose true when the criteria are met, FIXME when gaps are explicitly acknowledged in comments or tests with issue references or other identifying content, and false otherwise. It states the `FIXME(#125)` and `FIXME(rust-lang/rust#123)` convention and says references may occur elsewhere. It also asks for a rationale with source locations "including any acknowledged gaps".
- The reviewer-judgment obligations (grounding FIXME in recorded inputs, explaining the gaps and their locations, and not accepting a bare issue reference) live in the prompt text and in the harness recording supplied inputs. Validation deliberately does not reassess adequacy, per `requirements.ci.determination`.
- Other code marked `{impl}`: `index.rs` `LoadedDetailEvidence::load` (a thin wrapper over `load_path`) and `citations.rs` `validate` and `validate_review`. `validate_review` checks the citation-review determination with `Judgment::from_value` and reports false. The `{impl}` marks on `validate` and `load` are loose, since neither directly applies the outcome rules. They add no unspecified behavior.
- Callers outside the marked set apply the same shape check. `evidence.rs` `validate_evidence_file` and `authoring::submission` both call `Judgment::from_value`. They are marked for `ci.schema`, `ci.determination` and `authoring.submission`, and those requirements cite `ci.outcomes`. I did not reassess them. Their text does carry the outcomes shape: the schema requires `determination` to use one of the outcomes, and submission requires the three outcomes with nonempty FIXME entries.
- I found no code that implements part of this requirement without a mark and refers to it only by `{cite}`. The cites are in documentation chapters and examples.

**Tests**
- `tests/outcomes.rs::judgments_round_trip_and_reject_invalid_fixme_shapes` covers the three valid shapes, FIXME with an issue number, FIXME with free text, and 11 invalid shapes (boundaries and failures: empty array, blank entry, non-string entry, string instead of array, extra key, wrong case, null, and others).
- `src/authoring/mod.rs::submit_judgment_advertises_exactly_the_three_outcome_shapes` asserts the exact advertised schema.
- `initial_prompt_conveys_when_to_choose_each_outcome` asserts the guidance strings: the true, FIXME and false conditions, the `FIXME(#125)` convention, and "including any acknowledged gaps".
- `tests/outcomes.rs::fixture` and `malformed_fixme_is_invalid_and_reports_the_required_shape` show a malformed FIXME reported as invalid with the "nonempty array" message, and shown as Invalid in status.
- `tests/commands.rs::fixme_fixture` exercises FIXME judgments with issue references, URLs and free text end to end, and checks that they validate.
- `submissions_accept_exactly_a_judgment_and_a_nonempty_rationale` in the same file covers the same shape for submissions, though it is marked for `authoring.submission`, not this requirement.

The remaining reviewer-behaviour obligations (the model actually grounding FIXME, or choosing false for an unacknowledged additional gap) cannot be unit-tested deterministically. The prompt and schema tests cover what the harness controls.

I found no gaps and no FIXME acknowledgments.

text: :::{req} outcomes
A requirement or example judgment MUST use one of these outcomes, applying
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`:
- `true`: the sources support the subject and its testing obligations.
- `false`: the sources do not support the subject, or information is missing,
and the gaps are not all explicitly acknowledged in source comments or tests.
- `FIXME`: some aspects remain unmet or untested, and source comments or tests
explicitly acknowledge those gaps. The reviewer MUST explain the gaps and
their source locations in the rationale and record their issue references or
other identifying content from the inputs.
The JSON `determination` MUST be `true`, `false`, or an object containing exactly
`"FIXME"` with a nonempty array of nonempty strings, such as
`{"FIXME": ["#125", "rust-lang/rust#123"]}`. The expected source convention is
`FIXME(issue-number)`, for example `FIXME(#125)` or
`FIXME(rust-lang/rust#123)`. References MAY appear elsewhere in the comment or
test; the reviewer MUST recognize explicit acknowledgments without requiring
that spelling. When no issue reference is present, the strings MUST identify the
documented gap using its source content. A FIXME judgment MUST be grounded in
recorded evidence inputs; a bare issue reference without an acknowledged gap
MUST NOT suffice.
:::{req} review_criteria
The reviewer MUST assess the named subject using its text, referenced requirements,
and terminology definitions. For a requirement, the reviewer MUST assess whether
the code marked with `{impl}` implements every stated obligation completely and
exactly as stated, and whether its
tests cover the interesting cases in the design space, including relevant
boundaries and failure cases. The reviewer MUST also assess whether the
implementation is marked completely: code that implements part of the
requirement under {cite}`requirements.references.targets` without an `{impl}`
reference to it, including code that refers to it only with `{cite}`, MUST be
treated as a gap. Behavior in the `{impl}` code that the requirement does not
specify MUST be accounted for by another definition that the same code
implements; otherwise it MUST be treated as a gap. When another requirement implements part of the subject, the
reviewer MUST assess whether its text carries out that part, and MUST NOT
reassess its implementation, tests, or evidence; that requirement is assessed
separately. When there are no tests, the reviewer MUST assess whether the logic is
simple enough to need no test or a test is impractical to author, and explain that
judgment in the rationale.
For an example, the reviewer MUST assess whether tests exist whose setup and
assertions cover its scenario and expected outcomes. The rationale MUST identify
the relevant sources and explain the implementation and testing judgments for a
requirement, or the test coverage for an example. Referenced requirements provide
context; they MUST NOT become additional subjects to assess in full.
:::{definition} validation_error
:phrase: validation error
One message in a repository validation report, describing a single failed check.
It begins with the affected evidence file, requirement, or source location, names
the failed check, and states the specific missing, invalid, or changed value,
with the expected value when available. It is concise because agents are its
primary readers.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
